notes: The bus-request and bus-response record fields are treated as non-primary carriers where the rules bar record ports and fields from being primary; the register-stage instance paths use the specified black-box assumption.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> reg_stage_inst carries bus_req_i.addr through the register-stage instance.
points.reason: The instance receives the request address and its black-box output drives the forwarded address, so altering or withholding the request path can change or prevent the targeted access; confidentiality is not an objective for this concept.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_adr_o carries bus_req.addr to the held output assignment.
points.reason: The output directly exposes the request address to the external bus, so changing or withholding it can redirect or prevent the required access.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> reg_stage_inst carries bus_req_i.data into the register-stage instance.
points.reason: The instance receives and forwards the write payload, so the value can be observed or altered along this path; availability is not an objective for this concept.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_dat_o carries bus_req.data to the held output assignment.
points.reason: The output directly carries the write payload to the external bus, so it can disclose or alter the value being written.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> reg_stage_inst carries the rw, ben and stb request-control fields.
points.reason: The register-stage instance receives the transfer controls and forwards them, so they can be changed or withheld to alter or suppress the external operation.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> arbiter carries bus_req.lock and bus_req.stb into the pending-control process.
points.reason: The process uses the request strobe and lock state to set or retain pending and locked, which can change or block the transfer-control behavior.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_we_o carries bus_req.rw to the output assignment.
points.reason: The output directly determines external read versus write direction and can therefore be altered or withheld.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_sel_o carries bus_req.ben to the output assignment.
points.reason: The output directly determines the selected external byte lanes and can be changed to corrupt or prevent the intended transfer.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_stb_o carries bus_req.stb to the output assignment.
points.reason: The output directly qualifies the external transfer, so suppressing or asserting it changes whether the operation occurs.

points.reached by: arbiter ==> xbus_cyc_o carries pending, and reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_cyc_o carries bus_req.stb.
points.reason: The cycle output is formed from the request strobe and pending state, so changing either can redirect, terminate or block the external transfer.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> reg_stage_inst carries bus_req_i.src through the register-stage instance.
points.reason: The instance forwards the source identifier to the tag path, so changing it can corrupt downstream attribution; confidentiality and availability are not objectives for this concept.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_tag_o carries bus_req.src in tag bit 2.
points.reason: Tag bit 2 directly carries the source identifier, so changing the tag can cause downstream attribution or routing to be wrong.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> reg_stage_inst carries bus_req_i.priv and bus_req_i.debug through the register-stage instance.
points.reason: The instance forwards the privilege and debug attributes into the tag-generation path, so changing them can corrupt downstream access qualification.

points.reached by: reg_stage_inst ==> xbus_tag_o carries bus_req.priv and bus_req.debug through tag bit 0.
points.reason: The output tag bit is formed from privilege and debug attributes, so altering the tag or either contributing attribute can cause downstream authorization to be wrong.

points.reached by: xbus_dat_i ==> bus_rsp.data carries the external read data into the response-data assignment.
points.reason: The response-data logic receives xbus_dat_i and conditionally forwards it, so the returned value can be observed or altered; availability is not an objective for this concept.

points.reached by: bus_rsp.data ==> reg_stage_inst carries the response data into device_rsp_i, and reg_stage_inst ==> bus_rsp_o carries it upstream.
points.reason: The black-box register-stage instance receives and returns the response data, so the value can be observed or changed along that path; this uses the stated black-box assumption.

points.reached by: xbus_ack_i --> arbiter is tested to clear pending when the external operation completes.
points.reason: The acknowledgement input controls whether pending clears, so fabricating or suppressing it can prematurely complete or stall the request.

points.reached by: xbus_ack_i ==> bus_rsp.ack contributes directly to the response acknowledgement.
points.reason: The response acknowledgement is computed from xbus_ack_i and pending, so altering or withholding the input changes completion reporting or prevents it.

points.reached by: bus_rsp.ack ==> reg_stage_inst carries the completion result into the register-stage instance.
points.reason: The instance forwards the acknowledgement to the upstream response; under the black-box assumption, changing or blocking this path changes or delays completion.

points.reached by: xbus_err_i --> arbiter is tested to clear pending on an external error.
points.reason: The error input controls whether pending clears, so fabricating or suppressing it can abort, delay or otherwise corrupt the transaction result.

points.reached by: xbus_err_i ==> bus_rsp.ack contributes directly to the response acknowledgement.
points.reason: The response acknowledgement includes xbus_err_i, so changing the error indication changes completion reporting or can block it.

points.reached by: xbus_err_i ==> bus_rsp.err contributes directly to the response error status.
points.reason: The response error field is computed from xbus_err_i and pending, so the external error can be fabricated, hidden or prevented from being reported.

points.reached by: bus_rsp.ack ==> reg_stage_inst and bus_rsp.err ==> reg_stage_inst carry the error-related response status upstream.
points.reason: The black-box register-stage instance forwards the response status to bus_rsp_o, so altering or blocking this path changes or suppresses the reported error.

points.reached by: holding block
points.reason: This process stores the timeout counter and indication; altering the count or timeout decision can prematurely abort a transaction or prevent a stalled transaction from being released.

points.reached by: holding block
points.reason: This generate branch assigns timeout and timecnt constants based on the build-time generic, so the branch itself provides no run-time observation or influence mechanism.

points.reached by: timeout_counter --> arbiter and timeout_disabled --> arbiter carry timeout as a decision for pending.
points.reason: The timeout decision clears pending in the arbiter, thereby determining whether a stalled transaction remains active or is terminated.

points.reached by: timeout_counter ==> bus_rsp.ack and timeout_disabled ==> bus_rsp.ack carry timeout into the response acknowledgement.
points.reason: The timeout indication directly contributes to response acknowledgement, so changing it can fabricate completion or prevent a required completion report.

points.reached by: timeout_counter ==> bus_rsp.err and timeout_disabled ==> bus_rsp.err carry timeout into the response error.
points.reason: The timeout indication directly contributes to response error status, so changing it can fabricate or suppress timeout termination.

points.reached by: arbiter ==> xbus_cyc_o carries the pending state affected by timeout.
points.reason: Timeout can clear pending, which changes the external cycle and can prematurely end or prevent the bus operation.

points.reached by: bus_rsp.ack ==> reg_stage_inst and bus_rsp.err ==> reg_stage_inst carry timeout-derived status upstream.
points.reason: The black-box register-stage instance forwards timeout-derived acknowledgement and error status upstream, so the path can corrupt or block the timeout response.
